primitives.note: Spiked Shell converts 15% total armor + 15% total MR into bonus AD, continuously recalculated
Powerball channels then deals a single AoE collision burst; recastable early, auto-ends at 6s or on collision
Powerball is a channel that blocks other actions (except W/R interactions) until it collides or is recast
Defensive Ball Curl grants bonus armor/MR for 7s duration
W's return damage triggers only off attacks against Rammus; irrelevant in the damage fight where the dummy never attacks, only relevant in the survival fight as damage-taken interaction
Frenzying Taunt's monster damage is a fixed-target on-cast burst (only relevant vs monsters, not champion dummy)
Soaring Slam impact + 3 timed aftershocks (aftershocks reapply slow only, no stated damage)
Soaring Slam deals doubled damage to turrets (not applicable to a champion dummy) and merges with Powerball damage if cast mid-Q
Mana costs (Q60/W40/E50/R100) may matter over a 15s rotation depending on Rammus's mana pool at the tested level

needsBespoke.why: Rammus's core damage kit is almost entirely single-burst abilities with no repeatable on-hit rider beyond the passive AD conversion; the simulator needs to know P's continuous AD-from-resists conversion (recalculated as armor/MR change from W and items), Q's channel-then-single-AoE-burst-on-collision behavior (with an assumed 'always collides on cast' resolution against a stationary dummy), and R's conditional merge with Q's damage if cast during the Q channel. None of the listed primitives individually capture 'channel that deals its one damage instance upon collision with a stationary target that is always in range,' so the fight needs a bespoke rule: Q's collision is assumed to happen essentially immediately on cast against a stationary dummy (channel time before collision needs a ruling, see unsettled).

unsettled.question: Against a stationary target dummy, does Powerball collide (and deal its damage) immediately on cast, or only after some travel time since the dummy doesn't move and Rammus must roll into it?
options: Collision happens near-instantly since Rammus rolls toward the dummy and hits it almost immediately
Collision is delayed by whatever travel/pathing time the simulator assumes, effectively adding a cast-to-hit delay each time Q is used
Collision never happens automatically and requires the dummy to be adjacent at cast time
quotes: '''Rammus''' stops rolling upon colliding with an enemy, dealing {{as|magic damage}} to all nearby enemies

unsettled.question: After Powerball's initial collision burst, can Rammus re-cast Q again within the 15s fight to get a second collision-damage instance, or does the ability's post-effect cooldown-start plus recast/end behavior mean only one damage tick per cast is realistic?
options: Only one collision burst per Q cast (recast just ends the channel, no second damage)
The automatic recast after 6s if not manually ended could produce a second collision if Rammus is still moving/near the dummy, effectively creating a second damage window
quotes: ''Powerball'' can be recast after 1 second within the duration, and does so automatically afterwards

unsettled.question: If the rotation casts Soaring Slam (R) while Powerball (Q) is channeling, does the dummy (stationary, single target) actually receive the merged Powerball damage bonus, given the epicenter/knockup mechanic is designed for multiple enemies at range?
options: Yes — a single dummy standing at the impact epicenter takes both R's damage and Q's merged damage as two separate instances
No — this combo is positional/geometry-dependent (multi-hit shape) and should be treated as a positional assumption the dummy fight doesn't model, i.e., excluded from the baseline rotation
quotes: enemies within the epicenter of the impact are also {{tip|airborne|knocked up}} for {{fd|0.75}} seconds and are dealt ''{{ais|Powerball|Rammus}}'' damage

unsettled.question: Does Spiked Shell's bonus AD (15% armor + 15% MR) apply to on-hit/on-attack damage the same way normal bonus AD does, or is there any restriction (e.g., does it interact with AD ratios on abilities)?
options: It behaves as ordinary bonus AD, feeding into autoattack damage and any AD ratios
There is some special restriction not stated in either source
quotes: '''Rammus''' gains {{sti|{{as|'''bonus''' attack damage}}}} equal to the sum of {{as|15% '''total''' armor}} and {{as|15% '''total''' magic resistance}}.

unsettled.question: Is Frenzying Taunt's monster-only magic damage ever relevant to the champion-dummy damage fight (since the dummy 'counts as an enemy champion')?
options: No — dummy counts as champion, so E deals zero damage in the fight, it's purely a taunt with no damage output here
Some simulators might still credit the monster damage if the dummy is flagged as monster-like; sources don't clarify how the dummy is classified for this ability
quotes: Monsters are additionally dealt {{as|magic damage}} upon being affected.

proposal: Open by casting Q (Powerball) to roll toward the dummy and immediately trigger its magic damage burst on collision, then manually recast to end the channel and start its cooldown.

Cast E (Frenzying Taunt) on the dummy for the taunt (no damage vs a champion-classified dummy) mainly to keep on-cast effects like Spellblade active; otherwise skip if it contributes nothing to damage.
Cast R (Soaring Slam) on the dummy's location for its magic damage impact once available.

Cast W (Defensive Ball Curl) mainly for the passive AD gain via Spiked Shell (indirectly, since W boosts armor/MR which feeds P's AD conversion) between other casts; it contributes no direct damage against a non-attacking dummy.
Auto-attack the dummy continuously between ability casts to benefit from Spiked Shell's bonus AD.
Repeat Q on cooldown (6s minimum with rank 5) as the primary repeatable damage source, weaving auto-attacks in between.
Use R again if it comes off cooldown within the 15s window (rank 1 has 120s cooldown, so likely only cast once).
questions: Should E even be included in the rotation, given it apparently deals no damage to a champion-classified dummy and only provides a taunt (no CC benefit is scored)?

How does the simulator model Q's channel time before collision — does Rammus effectively deal Q's damage at time 0 of the cast, or after some fixed travel delay, and does that delay block auto-attacks during the channel?

Is W worth casting at all in the damage fight, given its own damage-dealing tooltip only fires off enemy attacks (which the dummy never performs), and its buff only matters via feeding Spiked Shell's AD conversion?
At what level/item state should R's single 120s-cooldown cast be assumed to land relative to the 15s fight window — always at t=0, or held for maximum stat scaling?
